key_insight: This paper shifts evaluation from only checking whether generated claims are correct to also checking whether they are complete. It introduces a two-level meta-rubric idea to systematically capture the full set of facts an ideal open-ended answer should include.
problem_solved: Current factuality evaluation methods are strong at catching wrong statements, but weak at identifying missing information in long-form generation. The paper tackles the harder problem of factual completeness: determining whether a response includes all required facts, not just correct ones.
method: Introduces GAMUT, a benchmark designed to evaluate factual completeness in open-ended generation.
Uses a two-level meta-rubric framework to organize required facts into structured evaluation criteria instead of a flat checklist.
Focuses on long-form answers where completeness depends on covering multiple nested or related factual points.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a more balanced way to evaluate generation quality beyond precision alone. It can improve benchmarking, model selection, and debugging for systems expected to produce thorough, trustworthy answers.

paper_title: Two-Level Meta-Rubrics for Evaluating Open-Ended Generation: GAMUT, a Benchmark for Factual Completeness
paper_authors: Xilun Chen, Zhaleh Feizollahi, Ross Goodwin, Seungwhan Moon, Scott Yih
